speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I wish I could report back to Parliament that things have got better for most breastfeeding mothers but hand on heart, I do not believe it has.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I sincerely believe that it will take a change in policies to be able to move the ground, shift mindsets and end the discrimination and stigma that breastfeeding mothers face.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In the past two years, I continue to hear stories of the challenges and difficulties breastfeeding mothers face at work.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The discrimination and stigma they face is real, the pain they feel is both on an emotional and physical level.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It is painful when their breasts become engorged from being unable to express their milk, the discriminatory words they hear are equally painful and they have to worry even about the quality of their breast milk.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Fion, a breastfeeding mother shared that, "I previously worked in a unit where chemicals are handled.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Unhealthy aerosols are in the air and there are no proper nursing rooms.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I remember using a corner of my manager's room, pantry or even the storage room just to express breast milk.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It did worry me that the environment will cause undesirable effects to the milk.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I was also disappointed when unkind remarks were passed due to special requests such as splitting my lunch hour so that I can pump breast milk.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Is it too much to ask for a clean and comfortable space with an understanding management team?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I'm just trying to feed my baby." This House must remember just that, that all these breastfeeding mothers are trying to do, is to feed their children.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We should do everything we can to help them fulfil this basic need.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: A few months ago, the Breastfeeding Mother's Support Group Singapore (BMSG) met with Government agencies to share their concerns and for the Prime Minister's Office, Ministry of National Development (MND), Ministry of Manpower (MOM) and Building and Construction Authority (BCA) to hear firsthand about the challenges and difficulties breastfeeding mothers face.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I saw a genuine concern from all the public servants in the room.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I went away from the meeting knowing that we have a team who are keen to provide a listening ear to understand the concerns on the ground and want to provide a helping hand and make positive changes.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Today, I will offer two recommendations on the positive changes breastfeeding mothers hope will be made.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I should first stress that my speech today is not about why breastfeeding is good.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Indeed, some mothers cannot or choose not to breastfeed and we should respect them all the same.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But we should note that an increasing number of mothers are breastfeeding and our policies and our physical environment have not kept pace.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: So, let me start by first sharing why there is not just a need for lactation rooms but that there is an increasing need for lactation rooms.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This lack of lactation rooms is a growing problem.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In February this year, the Health Promotion Board (HPB) and maternity hospitals reported breastfeeding as being on the rise.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Among infants from birth to under six months, nearly 40% of infants were exclusively breastfed.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: A Nielsen IQ Baby Power 2022 study showed that women are nursing their babies for an average of 11.8 months in 2022.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This is an increase from 8.1 months in 2018.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The data very importantly shows that many mothers continue to breastfeed after their maternity leave of four months is over.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Lactation rooms are not a luxury, but something which all working mothers who are breastfeeding desperately need.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In a survey of 971 mothers conducted by BMSG in 2022, eight in 10 mothers shared that a lactation room would be one of the most useful forms of workplace support.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The first two problems are the threshold and the minimum requirement of only one lactation room.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In September 2023, in response to my Parliamentary Question, Minister Desmond Lee shared that there are around 3,950 offices that are below 10,000 square metres in GFA and only 300 offices that are above 10,000 square metres in GFA.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This means that the vast majority of offices are not required to provide a lactation room.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: On the ground, breastfeeding mothers directly face this lack of lactation rooms.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In a survey conducted by BMSG in August last year of around 370 nursing mothers, the majority of respondents shared that their working location does not have dedicated facilities for nursing mothers to breastfeed or express milk.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Respondents shared a variety of locations that they have used to express milk instead.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: These included at their desk, meeting rooms, storerooms and even sadly toilets.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: One mother shared, "Currently, there is no private room that can be used for pumping so the only option is to pump in the toilet if I go to office.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I am quite concerned about the hygiene and inconvenience caused to other colleagues as they cannot use the toilet while I am pumping." The need for lactation rooms is real and for many larger buildings, clearly more than one lactation room is needed.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: One mother shared, "There are many occasions that I have to wait 30 to 40 minutes to use the only nursing room in a six-storey building." Expressing breastmilk does take time and many breastfeeding mothers do not have the luxury of time to queue.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The last problem is that we do not even have sufficient proper standards for lactation rooms.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It is not even mandated in the Code that the lactation room is lockable, and in those cases, a mother would constantly fear that someone might walk into the room during what is a very vulnerable moment for them.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We must remember again that this lack of proper lactation rooms reinforces workplace norms against breastfeeding.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It reinforces the discrimination and stigma that breastfeeding mothers face.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The problems I have highlighted can be solved and I am glad many are stepping forward on their own to provide help.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: There are many who have gone above and beyond the minimum requirements to provide lactation rooms and with better facilities.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I had the opportunity to visit one of their offices with four lactation rooms in a single building.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Their lactation rooms were lockable and available for use through a booking system.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: They also came with a dedicated fridge and freezer, electrical sockets, comfortable armchairs, sinks and water dispensers.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Many others have taken similar steps to support breastfeeding mothers.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: That is indeed good news, but the reality is that for many building owners, it will take a change in the Code on Accessibility in the Built Environment before a lactation room is provided or more lactation rooms are provided with better facilities.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: As such, the call today is for building owners who have more resources than SMEs to provide the lactation rooms.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: As mentioned, the Code requires only at least one lactation room in offices and business parks of 10,000 square metres or more in GFA.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We need to ensure that the Code applies to the majority of offices and business parks rather than the small minority which is currently the case.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: A single lactation room in a building above 10,000 square metres in GFA is also just not sufficient.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: So many mothers have shared stories about rushing to a lactation room during their lunch break only to find that another mother is already using it.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: One mother shared with BMSG that she has had to wait 15 to 30 minutes outside a lactation room as a mother was already pumping inside.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Another mother told me that she would sometimes only have five minutes left for her own lunch after expressing her milk.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: No mother should have to choose between feeding herself or her child.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It is also clear again that buildings with more occupants have higher needs.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In fact, the Code already recognises that this as it states that "the number of lactation rooms to be provided should be based on the scale of the building and the needs of the building users".

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Again, I propose that we peg the number of lactation rooms to the size of the building by requiring at least one lactation room per 2,500 square metres in GFA.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: MND has said that the GFA threshold is a base guideline meant to strike a balance between needs and the efficient use of space, and that some buildings go beyond these requirements.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Indeed, as Senior Minister of State Zaqy Mohamad shared when we debated this issue four years ago, MND itself has two lactation rooms in the MND Headquarters within the floors they occupied while MOM has five in its two office buildings.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I appreciate the Government going above and beyond for its employees and the Government clearly recognises the need.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But what about all the women not working for the Government?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I should remind this House that the pain breastfeeding mothers feel is not just on an emotional level but physically as well.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: When a breastfeeding mother fails to pump at the right time, their breasts can become swollen and create sharp, burning pains.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Breastfeeding mothers need help and we should change our policies to provide this help.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Under the existing Code, there is a list of nine items a lactation room should be equipped with.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: These are comfortable sitting, diaper changing stations, waste bins for disposing used diapers, wash basins with liquid detergent and paper towels, dispensers for hot and cold water, vending machines for beverages and diapers, socket outlets for breast pumps, mirrors and refrigerators with freezers for milk storage.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: These standards sound very good, but it is only stated that these items "should be" rather than "must be" provided.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Furthermore, the Code only requires lactation rooms in workplaces to have three out of the nine items.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: These are comfortable sitting, socket outlets for breast pumps and refrigerators with freezers.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The Code also only states that a lockable cubicle is preferred, but not mandated.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Should this not be the most important feature to mandate?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We need mandatory standards so that all mothers are assured that when they see a lactation room, it is able to serve its purpose.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Many of these facilities, such as a waste bin, water dispenser, mirror and a lock are, in fact, very basic.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: They do not require significant additional cost for building owners to provide.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In the BMSG survey, mothers have stated that the above features are important in a lactation room.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I hope MND will review the Code with the recommendations of breastfeeding mothers in mind and mandate more facilities in lactation rooms in workplaces.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I recognise that not all building owners are able to immediately meet higher standards or provide more lactation rooms.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I hope MND can implement these new standards progressively.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Lastly, there is the option of installing lactation pods which will be much faster and easier to install as compared to constructing a lactation room.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Some have asked why provide it when there might not be breastfeeding mothers in the office currently?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The issue here is not just about providing a physical space but about shifting mindsets, removing stigma and ending the discrimination.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In this day and age, we do not ask why there is a need to provide an accessible toilet.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We recognise that our buildings should be inclusive in making sure that accessible toilets are widely available, even if some buildings may not have adults with disabilities or seniors.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We have used this Code to shift mindsets when it comes to adults with disabilities or seniors.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: For them, we have used this code to ensure that we are inclusive.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Why the disparity when it comes to breastfeeding mothers?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We should use the same Code to now shift mindsets, remove stigma and end the discrimination breastfeeding mothers face.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I first learnt about the difficulties that breastfeeding mothers face when it was raised at my public dialogue session in February 2020.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In the past four years, I have spoken repeatedly about this in this House.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I have filed many Parliamentary Questions and I have pushed hard for positive changes.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My efforts in this House have really been made possible by the tremendous work done by the Breastfeeding Mothers' Support Group Singapore both in the background and in the forefront.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It has been a privilege working with them in the past four years.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: So, let me end by thanking the Breastfeeding Mothers' Support Group Singapore, led by Elaine, for speaking up and fighting hard for all breastfeeding mothers.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Many of them, including Elaine, are here with us this evening and are sitting in the Gallery.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: They continue to wish that we move towards embracing rather than just tolerating breastfeeding.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: They have waited for a long time and I hope we finally fulfil their wish.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Not because I think less of formula feeding moms.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Not because I want to show my breasts to others.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I breastfeed Because I couldn't imagine it any other way.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Because my child wants to be nourished from me.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Because this was the right choice for my family."

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Women are a crucial part of the workforce and it is important that workplaces cater to their needs.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: For many mothers who have recently given birth, the transition back to work can be challenging, as they have to care for their babies while managing their work responsibilities.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Medical research has highlighted the benefits of breast milk for babies.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: As Mr Ng has pointed out, the number of mothers choosing to breastfeed is increasing with some mothers continuing to do so even after returning to work.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Given that women form a significant part of our workforce and many continue working even after childbirth, it is important that our workplaces are supportive of mothers.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This is especially so in light of our low total fertility rate (TFR).

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Our workplaces can support mothers by providing a clean and conducive environment for breastfeeding mothers to express milk, so they can meet their babies' needs, even as they resume work.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: As mentioned in my reply to Mr Ng's last Adjournment Motion on this topic, we have progressively introduced measures over the years to support breastfeeding mothers.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We conducted substantive reviews of the Code on Accessibility in the Built Environment in 2013 and 2019.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The Accessibility Fund co-funds the construction cost of accessibility features, including lactation rooms, to encourage building owners and employers to install them.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In 2022, we expanded the scope of the Accessibility Fund to two additional categories of private sector buildings.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: First, buildings that were built before 1990 and were already equipped with basic accessibility features.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Second, buildings which were built after 1990, but before the implementation of the 2013 Code and which provided fewer accessibility features than required under the pre-2013 Code.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The Government will continue to support breastfeeding mothers in two key areas.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: First, by reviewing the relevant legislation and incentives for the provision of lactation facilities; and second, by promoting an inclusive, supportive work culture for breastfeeding mothers.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: BCA has formed a Code Review Committee, comprising public and private sector stakeholders, with representation from 15 organisations, including social service agencies, industry associations and Government agencies.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: A key focus of the review is on lactation rooms.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Their frank and generous sharing of their experiences has enabled the Committee to better understand the needs of and the challenges faced by breastfeeding mothers.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The current Code requires buildings, such as offices and business parks, with 10,000 square metres or more in GFA to provide at least one lactation room.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We are encouraged that several progressive building owners and employers have provided lactation rooms beyond these minimum requirements.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: JEM and CapitaSpring are examples of larger developments that have voluntarily provided more than one lactation room.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Some developments with GFA of less than 10,000 square metres, including some hawker centres, have also provided lactation rooms voluntarily.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Nonetheless, we agree that there is scope to lower the GFA thresholds in the Code for the installation of lactation rooms in offices and business parks and to consider requiring larger buildings to install more lactation rooms.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: I wish to reassure Mr Louis Ng that the Committee is studying this issue carefully.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We need to take a calibrated and balanced approach, bearing in mind the other competing needs for space within developments and the constraints of smaller developments.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The Committee will consider these issues when making its recommendations on the GFA thresholds for lactation rooms.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In the meantime, I wish to highlight that specially constructed lactation rooms are not the only solution to meeting breastfeeding mothers' need for private space.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Lactation pods are a viable alternative for owners of or employers in buildings with lower GFA or with configuration constraints.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: These pods are commercially available for purchase or lease and the pod exterior can be customised to align with the office branding or décor.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: I urge employers in and owners of smaller buildings or buildings with limited space to consider installing lactation pods.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The Accessibility Fund can be tapped on to co-fund lactation pods.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: But beyond just providing lactation rooms, it is important that lactation rooms are sufficiently equipped to meet the needs of breastfeeding mothers, as Mr Ng has pointed out.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The Code currently recommends a list of items that all lactation rooms should be equipped with.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We note Mr Ng's suggestions for more items to be added to the list.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Moving forward, we can consider making some essential features of a lactation room mandatory.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: For instance, privacy, easy access and access to electricity.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: At the same time, we must be mindful about striking the right balance.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Employers and building owners need also sufficient flexibility in determining how to address the needs of other building users.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: For instance, they may wish to site loose fixtures and appliances, such as water dispensers in common locations like pantries.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Modalities may differ from site to site, but what matters is that there is thoughtful provision of facilities to meet employees' needs, including those of breastfeeding mothers.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The Code Review Committee will continue to assess this and continue to gather data to refine its proposed enhancements to the Code.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We need to go beyond mandatory infrastructural provisions and encourage progressive workplaces that benefit both the employee and the employer.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Millennials and Gen Z have very different expectations towards work and workplaces.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: There is keen competition for workers and talent, including female workers.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Bosses who are empathetic and who can balance business objectives with employee needs, will have a strategic advantage in recruitment and retention.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This includes developing a workplace culture that supports motherhood and breastfeeding.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Fostering such an inclusive workplace culture ultimately requires mutual support among supervisors, colleagues and the wider community.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: It also requires capable human resources (HR) personnel, good HR practices and above all, candid conversations between employers and employees, and a collaborative effort to meet the needs of both.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Everyone has a part to play in building a workplace culture of mutual trust so that all employees, including breastfeeding mothers, can give their best both at work and at home.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Together with our tripartite partners, the Government encourages employers to adopt family-friendly workplace practices.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The standards involve implementing good workplace practices to support employees in managing their work responsibilities and personal lives effectively.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In today's world, prospective hires do not only look at a company's business outcomes but also at the progressiveness of its HR practices and workplace culture.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: I hope employers will view progressive practices, including facilities for breastfeeding mothers, as investments into employee well-being that will in turn benefit all.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We are reviewing the Code, including the areas highlighted by Mr Ng.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We will also continue to work with our tripartite partners to promote family-friendly practices.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We will need all stakeholders, including building owners, employers and colleagues, to play their part.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: With this collective effort, we can build a Singapore Made For Families.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Minister, you have less than two minutes to respond.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The answer, Mr Speaker, is that we always take Mr Ng's recommendations seriously.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Because if it mandates more, then employers and building owners may need more assistance.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, we have to size the Accessibility Fund depending on what we require them to do.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: And I can see smiles and happy faces in the Chamber and up in the Gallery.
